questions.q: What is ADF's core unit generally organized around?
options: Movement between systems — activities like Copy, Lookup, or Web, wired together visually
Code-based transformation logic written directly in PySpark
An inferred dependency graph from function references
Row-level and column-level security masks
questions.explain: This contrasts with Lakeflow's declarative pipeline, organized primarily around transformation within Databricks.

questions.q: Where does row-level casting, deduplication, or business aggregation typically actually happen in an ADF-based workflow?
options: In a Databricks notebook activity called by ADF, or in Lakeflow's own @dlt.table functions — not in the Copy Activity itself
Directly inside the Copy Activity, which handles both movement and transformation
ADF cannot perform any transformation logic anywhere in its pipelines
It always happens in a separate on-premises SQL Server
questions.explain: An ADF Copy Activity moves bytes; the actual transformation logic lives elsewhere.

questions.q: What does the combined ADF + Lakeflow pattern described in this lesson look like?
options: ADF copies data from a system Databricks can't reach directly into a landing zone, then triggers a Lakeflow Pipeline task for the actual transformation work
ADF and Lakeflow can never be used together in the same organization
Lakeflow always replaces ADF entirely once adopted
ADF only triggers Lakeflow pipelines, never moves any actual data
questions.explain: This reuses Lesson 54's Pipeline task type as the actual handoff point.

questions.q: Why is "ADF or Lakeflow" often the wrong question for a real organization using both?
options: The real question is which tool is doing which job — ADF for movement between systems, Lakeflow for transformation within Databricks — in a pipeline that may legitimately use both
Because ADF has been fully deprecated in favor of Lakeflow
Because Lakeflow cannot move data between any systems at all
Because the two tools are functionally identical, making the choice arbitrary
questions.explain: Neither tool disappears when both are used — each does what it's actually better at.

questions.q: When would ADF be the right tool to reach for, according to this lesson?
options: For moving data between many different, often non-Databricks systems, like an on-prem database or a legacy FTP server
For writing complex, code-based transformation logic like casting and deduplication
For defining row-level security masks on a Delta table
For declaring a table's dependency graph via function references
questions.explain: Complex, code-based transformation logic is where Lakeflow is the better fit instead.
